AEDT definition: computational process using ML/AI that issues simplified output to substantially assist or replace discretionary employment decision-making
Auditor must not be employed by, have financial interest in, or have been involved in developing the AEDT within past three years
Notice to promotion candidates must be provided at least 10 business days before AEDT use
Public disclosure of bias audit summary with all required data elements on employment section of website
Civil penalties of $500-$1,500 per violation; each candidate screening may be a separate violation
Notice must include instructions for requesting alternative process but employer not required to provide one
Prohibits AI deployment with intent to unlawfully discriminate; requires intentional discrimination not mere disparate impact
AI disclosure obligations apply only to government agencies, not private employers
Deployers must complete impact assessments before deployment and annually thereafter
Deployers must provide consumer notice before consequential decisions and offer appeal rights
Scoring AEDT bias audit must calculate median score, scoring rates, and impact ratios across sex, race/ethnicity, and intersectional categories

PromoteAI is a computational process that generates a simplified output (0-100 composite score) used to rank promotion candidates. It uses machine-based techniques to generate predictions about candidate fitness. The score is used to substantially assist discretionary decision-making for promotions (an employment decision) within NYC. All elements of the AEDT definition are met.

The most recent bias audit was completed March 2025. The May 2026 promotion cycle is more than 14 months later, exceeding the one-year maximum under Section 20-871(a)(1) and DCWP Rules Section 5-301(a). Metropolitan may not use PromoteAI for the May 2026 cycle without a new audit.

Compliance Analytics Group has no employment relationship with Metropolitan, no financial interest in Metropolitan, and was not involved in developing PromoteAI (which was built internally by Metropolitan IT). All three independence prongs are satisfied.
Notice is sent 3 business days before the promotion cycle. DCWP Rules Section 5-304(c) requires at least 10 business days. The notice is 7 business days short of the minimum requirement.

The bias audit summary is posted on the careers page in a clearly labeled section, satisfying the location and conspicuousness requirements. However, the facts do not confirm whether all required data elements are included: distribution date, data source explanation, unknown category counts, applicant numbers, scoring rates, and impact ratios. Compliance is partial pending verification of content completeness.

No facts establish Metropolitan operates in Texas. Even if TRAIGA applied, it only prohibits intentional discrimination and imposes no audit, notice, or assessment requirements on private employers. No facts suggest intentional discriminatory intent. No violation.
TRAIGA Section 551.101 disclosure obligations apply only to government agencies. Metropolitan is a private health system. No disclosure obligation exists under TRAIGA.

Colorado AIA is not in force until June 30, 2026. No current binding obligation exists. Whether Metropolitan must comply depends on whether it does business in Colorado, which is not established in the facts. If applicable, it would need impact assessments within 90 days of the effective date for already-deployed systems.

Each use of a non-compliant AEDT to screen a single candidate is a separate violation. With 22,000 employees and multiple nursing promotion candidates, Metropolitan faces per-candidate penalties of $500-$1,500 for each of the stale audit, deficient notice content, and deficient notice timing violations.

PromoteAI is a scoring AEDT, so the bias audit must follow DCWP Rules Section 5-301(c) requirements for scoring AEDTs: median score calculation, scoring rates, and impact ratios across sex, race/ethnicity, and intersectional categories. The facts state the audit evaluated impact on these categories but do not confirm all scoring-specific calculations were performed.
